sentences.text: J U D G M E N T

The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/S.166 of M.V. Act against the respondents claiming compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petition are as under:
On 29.3.2017 at about 7.30 p.m. the petitioner was a pedestrian walking on the Kanakapura main road in front of Rajegowda Military hotel, at that time the driver of the car bearing No.KA-01-AF-8018 came from the opposite direction with high speed in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human lie and safety of others and dashed against the petitioner.
Consequent to the terrific impact, the petitioner was fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately the petitioner was shifted to Sagar hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took the first aid treatment, thereafter he was shifted to NIMHANS and then he was referred to Victoria hospital and again he was shifted to Chaya Medical Centre, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient.

3. Further the contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, she was hale and healthy,
aged about 14 years, studying in 7th standard at New Mother land School, Avalahalli, Bengaluur.
On account of the injuries he could not attend the class and lost one academic year.
The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car.
Therefore, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Contending the above facts, he prays to grant for compensation with interest and cost.
4. In response to the petition notice, the respondent No.1 has not appeared before the court, placed exparte.
The respondent No.2 has appeared before the court through its counsel and filed its respective written statement.
5. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 are as under:
The respondent No.2 in its written statement averred that, the claim petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

Further contended that Master Shaik Faisal @ Faisal vs M/S Voler Car Pvt. Ltd on 21 August, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109505988/
2 neither the owner of the vehicle nor the jurisdictional police have complied mandatory provisions u/s 134 and S.158 (6) of the MV Act.

sentences.text: Further contended that the driver of the offending vehicle had valid and effective driving licence to drive the above said vehicle as on the date of accident.
Further admitted about the issuance of the policy in respect of vehicle bearing No.KA-01-AF-8018 and its validity.

Further contended that accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner alone, who while trying to cross the busy Kanakapura main road, where there is no provision for pedestrians to cross the said road and suddenly he came to the middle of the road and running negligently in a abrupt manner and caused the accident.
Further denied the age avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in the claim petition.
Contending the above facts, prays to dismiss the claim petition with cost.

6. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Sports Car bearing No.KA-01-AF-8018 on 29.3.2017 at about 7.30 p.m. near Rajegowda Military Hotel, Kanakapura Main Road, Banashankari, Bengaluru?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3
. What order or award?

7. In order to prove the case, the father of the petitioner has examined as PW1 and got marked the documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P12 and doctor is examined as PW2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P13 & Ex.P14.
8. To disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove the defence, the respondent has examined official of the RTO as RW1 and got marked the document at Ex.R1 & Ex.R2.
9. Heard the arguments.

10. My findings to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: In the Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per final order for the following:
R E A S O N S 11. ISSUE NO.1:- During the course of arguments, the learned counsel for the petitioner argued by reiterating the contents of petition and also evidence put forth by PW1 & PW2.
Further he argued that, the petitioner has proved his case as contended in the petition by producing oral and documentary evidence.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.

sentences.text: Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has argued by denying the manner of the accident as alleged in the petition and contended that accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner alone, who while trying to cross the busy Kanakapura main road, where there is no provision for pedestrians to cross the said road and suddenly he came to the middle of the road and running negligently in a abrupt manner and caused the accident.

Accordingly, he prays to dismiss the petition as against the respondent No.2.
13.
On rival contention urged by both the counsel, I, intend to discuss the merits of the case.
14. In order to prove the case, the father of the petitioner has examined as P.W.1 and he has stated in his evidence by reiterating the contents of petition.

To substantiate the said contention he has produced prosecution papers and the same are marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P6 such as FIR with Complaint, mahazar, Sketch, IMV report, wound certificate and charge sheet respectively.
15. On perusal of complaint marked at Ex.P1 reveals that, complaint has been lodged by one Mubarak Pasha on 30.3.2017.

Based on the complaint FIR marked at Ex.P1 has been registered against the driver of the car in Cr.No.80/2017 by Bhanashankari Traffic police for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337 of IPC and S.134(A) & (B) of IMV Act.
Ex.P2 is the spot mahazar and Ex.
P3 is the sketch also reveals the scene of occurrence and then it corroborate the evidence of PW1 &
PW2 , Ex.P4 is IMV report also reveals the damages caused to the vehicle and IMV inspector has opined that accident was not occurred due to any mechanical defect of the vehicle.

Ex.P5 is the wound certificate reveals the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident and on perusal of charge sheet at Ex.P6 reveals that after investigation I.O. has filed charge sheet against the offending vehicle driver for the offences punishable U/s 279 and 338 of IPC and S. 134 (A & B) of IMV Act.

16 . The counsel for the respondent No.2 has argued that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner alone, who while trying to cross the busy Kanakapura main road, where there is no provision for pedestrians to cross the said road and suddenly he came to the middle of the road and running negligently in a abrupt manner and caused the accident.
To substantiate the said fact, he has not examined any witness or produced any documents to show that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner.
On the other hand, petitioner has proved his case through oral and documentary evidence.

17. In addenda of this, in a claim for compensation U/S.166 of MV Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others Vs. Satbir and others).

sentences.text: 18. Looking to the oral evidence of PW1 and the documents placed before the court I am of the opinion that, petitioner has proved her case that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-01-AF-8018.
Hence, I answer this issue in the affirmative.

Immediately he was taken to Sagar hospital, wherein he took the first aid treatment, later on he was shifted to NIMHANS and then he was referred to Victoria hospital and again he was shifted to Chaya Medical Centre and took the treatment as inpatient.

To substantiate the said fact, PW1 has produced wound certificate at Ex.P5, which reveals the following injuries;
1) CLW over right parietal region, multiple facial abrasions and Head injury 20.
The doctor is of the opinion that the injury is grievous in nature.
PW1 has produced Ex.

21. PW2 being the Neuro Rehabilitation at Deepashree Hospital has stated in his evidence that petitioner has sustained mild head injury, -clean lacerated wound over right parietal injury 10 C X 1 cms with multiple facial abrasions and hip abrasions with asymmetrical vessel injury.
He has produced Ex.P13 and Ex.P14 such as Examination report and Neuropsychological assessment report.

Considering the oral evidence of PW1 and PW2 and the documents placed before the court, I am of the opinion that the petitioner might have sustained pain and agony, for which, she is entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of pain and sufferings.
22. The case of the petitioner is that, he was hale and healthy at the time of accident, aged about 14 years.
Due to the accidental injuries he has suffered a lot.
PW1 has produced Ex.P10 discharge summary, which reveals that the petitioner was admitted on 31.3.2017 and discharged on 5.4.2017.
During the said period either father or mother, one has to look after their son by leaving their work.
So, I deem it fit to grant Rs.20,000/- under the head of inconvenience caused to the parents during the treatment period.
Therefore, Rs.20,000/- is granted to the petitioner under this head.
23. The contention of PW1 is that, they have spent Rs.50,000/- towards medical expenses.

He has produced the medical bills at Ex.P12 to the extent of Rs30,947/- supported with prescriptions, I deem it just and reasonable to grant compensation of Rs.30,947/- under the head of medical expenses.

24. Further contention of the PW1 is that, prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy,
aged about 14 years, student.
Due to the accidental injuries, he has became permanent disability as he cannot stand in sunlight, headache, giddiness, slurring speech, he cannot do his normal activities.

Further stated that prior to the accident the petitioner was studying in 7th standard at New Mother Land School, avalahalli, Begnaluur , due to the accident the petitioner could not attend class and lost one academic year.

sentences.text: He is referred for neuropsychological assessment.

He has produced Neuropsychological report marked at Ex.P14, in which it reveals the following;
"There are no parietal focal signs present on testing.
Confabulation is present across the tests.
Personality changes in the form of sad mood and irritability is present.
On the tests measured he shows deficits in Execution functions indicating involvement of the frontal cortex.
Deficits in verbal fluency indicate left frontal involvement of the following area is seen on impaired.
Performance on working memory, deficits in verbal learning and memory, visual learning and memory are indicative of a bilateral temporal lobe involvement.

As learning is inadequate for both verbal and visual tasks, it indicates the involvement of prefrontal cortices."
26.
Based on the said report PW2 has assessed the whole body disability as 26.66%.
On perusal of cross-examination of PW2 he has stated that the physical activities of the petitioner are normal and now there is no treatment.
Looking to the age of the petitioner the percentage f the disability may comedown.
Further he has admitted that he has not aware prior condition of the petitioner before the accident.

27. At this juncture this court has relied the decision reported in 2013 ACJ 2445 in between Mallikarjun vs. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Co.Ltd.,and another, which reads like thus;
Quantum - Injury - Principles of assessment - Assessment of compensation in case of children suffering disability - Apex Court observed that appropriate compensation on all other heads in addition to the actual expenditure for treatment, attendant, etc., should be, if the disability is above 10 per cent and up to 30 per cent to the whole body, Rs.3,00,000; up to 60 percent, Rs.4,00,000; up to 90 per cent, Rs.5,00,000 and above 90 per cent, it should be Rs.6,00,000; for permanent disability up to 10 per cent, it should be Rs.1,00,000, unless there are exceptional circumstances to take a different yardstick.

sentences.text: 28. So, looking to the age of the petitioner and the relative disability, the disability of the petitioner shall be considered as 10% of whole body.
Therefore, Rs.1,00,000/- is granted under the head of disability.

On perusal of Ex.P8 discharge summary, which reveals that the petitioner was admitted on 31.3.2017 and discharged on 5.4.2017.
So, one must attend him during the above said period.

So, considering the above facts, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.15,000/-under the head of amenities, attendant, conveyance, food and nourishment etc.,

He ha stated in his evidence that the driver of the offending vehicle viz., Anjan had licence to drive LMV (Non-Transport) and motor cycle with gear and there is no endorsement.
As per Ex.R2 the driver had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle.

sentences.text: In the instant case, the driver of the offending vehicle had licence to drive LMV (Non-Transport).
So, as on the date of accident he was driving a car bearing No.KA-01-AF-8018.
As per citation the gross weight does not exceed 7,500 Kgs.
Therefore, LMV holder can drive unladen weight up to 7,500/- kgs.
no separate endorsement on the licence is required to drive a transport vehicle of light motor vehicle class.
Therefore, arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 cannot be accepted.
37. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has admitted about the issuance of the policy in respect of car bearing No. KA-01-AF-8018 and its validity.
Therefore, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 alone is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner with interest @ 8% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answer the issue No.2 in the partly affirmative.
38. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of above discussion on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of MV Act as against the respondents is partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,05,947/- with interest @ 8% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance police the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner with interest at 8% p.a. from the date of petition till its realisation within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of compensation amount together with interest, entire amount shall be kept in FD in the name of petitioner in any nationalized/schedule bank till he attains age of majority and after attaining the age of majority the entire amount shall be released to the petitioner through account payee cheque on proper identification without any further proceedings.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
